findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following were observed.
1. The caulking sealing the countertop left of the dish machine was observed undone.
2. A buildup of soil accumulations was observed beneath the grill. 
3. A buildup of dust and soil on the fan in the walk-in cooler.

Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspector that the relevant cleaning and repairs will be done. Ensure that the buildups are cleaned and the caulking re-done providing smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:

Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Inspector observed a jug of milk in the chest cooler in the serving area not properly date marked. Discussed with PIC. PIC confirm that the milk jug was open the day prior (11/12/2025). PIC instructed a staff member to date mark the milk jug. Education was carried out. Ensure that ready to eat food and TCS food are properly date marked if they are going to be store for more than 24 hours after opening or prep. 

Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15(A) Inspector observed the screen door at the back exit to not be tightly fitted to the frame. Inspector observed visible light passing through the top of the screen door. PIC was made aware. Ensure that this door is repaired to be tightly fitting to properly seal off the doorway at the back exit in order to discourage the entry of pests. 

Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Facility was observed to be out of compliance with food allergen awareness training. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the training will be done. Ensure that facility is compliant with this law. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.

findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (1) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before each use with a different type of raw animal FOOD such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, or POULTRY; (2) Each time there is a change from working with raw FOODS to working with READY-TO-EAT FOODS; (3) Between uses with raw fruits and vegetables and with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD; (4) Before using or storing a FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE; and (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Facility is not compliant with the food handler law. Discussed  with PIC and PIC was not knowledgeable about whether the employee had valid food handler certifications. Ensure that employee handling foo acquire their food handler certifications. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The shelving used to store the pans and spare utensils is observed to be visibly soiled with grease and food debris. All of the pans need to be removed from the shelving and placed into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. While these items are removed from the shelves, the shelving units need to be cleaned and sanitized before placing the pans back onto the shelves, especially the surfaces that come into contact with the lip portion of the stored items. Ensure that the food contact surface of stored pans and the shelving used to store them are kept clean and sanitized. A follow-up will take place on September 16, 2024 to observe the progress on this cleaning and sanitizing process. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.112: There are several dead roaches observed along the walls of the back storage room, the hallway leading to the storage room, and along the walls/under equipment near the dish/triple sink areas. The facility has been treated by Sentinel since the previous inspection which has caused an increase in the quantity observed carcasses. Ensure that as treatment takes place that dead insects are removed from the facility at a frequency necessary to prevent accumulation. 
6-501.112: Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-801.11: There was observed an employee to use their bare hands to dish out a food item into a single service container. This behavior was corrected on site and the employee was educated to use a utensil or a gloved hand to handle RTE foods. Ensure employees are educated on using a barrier of some kind and to not bare hand RTE food items. 
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under  3-301.11(B) and (E).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The shelving used to store the pans and spare utensils is observed to be visibly soiled with grease and food debris. All of the pans need to be removed from the shelving and placed into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. While these items are removed from the shelves, the shelving units need to be cleaned and sanitized before placing the pans back onto the shelves, especially the surfaces that come into contact with the lip portion of the stored items. Ensure that the food contact surface of stored pans and the shelving used to store them are kept clean and sanitized. A follow-up will take place on March 8, 2024 to observe the progress on this cleaning and sanitizing process. This is a repeat violation from the 2/27/2024 original inspection. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: There are observed several live roaches in the kitchen near the triple sink and dish areas. Roaches of varying stages of the life cycle were observed. Ensure pest control is contacted and that the facility is treated before the follow-up taking place on September 6, 2024. 
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.112: There are several dead roaches observed along the walls of the back storage room, the hallway leading to the storage room, and along the walls/under equipment near the dish/triple sink areas. Ensure that the currently dead insects are cleaned and removed from the facility. Ensure that as treatment takes place that dead insects are removed from the facility at a frequency necessary to prevent accumulation. 
6-501.112: Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: There was observed a wiping cloth being stored on the surface of the prep table. This cloth was removed from this location and placed into the sanitizer bucket to be held fully submerged between uses. Ensure that wiping cloths are held fully submerged in the sanitizer solution between uses. 
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: The gaskets of the walk-in freezer and the walk-in cooler are observed in a state of disrepair. Ensure the current gaskets are removed and replaced/repaired to create a seal that is smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable and that allows the doors to shut completely with no visible gaps. 
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The shelves holding pans in the narrow hallway are observed to have an accumulation of soil debris/grease accumulation. See violation #16 regarding the pans. Ensure the shelving units are cleaned and sanitized to remove the current soils and then cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. This is a repeat violation from the 2/27/2024 original inspection and the facility will receive a Warning Letter to document the violation. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: There are old and new mouse droppings observed in the following locations:
-Dry storage room under the shelving.
-In the storage room leading to the dry storage room.
-Under the shelving storing pans in the narrow hallway.
Ensure the old and new mouse droppings are cleaned from the facility. The cleaning of these items will help to protect the public’s health and also allow for better monitoring of the pest issue in the facility to help determine how active of a pest issue is present in the facility.
This violation is a repeat from the 9/26/2023 and 2/27/2024 inspections and the facility will receive a Notice to Correct documenting this occurrence.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: There is observed a crack in the wall under the back room triple sink. This crack needs to be repaired to make it smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable. 
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The floor behind the cooking equipment is observed to be heavily soiled with grease and food debris. Ensure that these areas are cleaned to remove the current accumulation of grease/debris and then cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.
